title: Missing values
summary: Find and handle missing bike trip data. Fill blanks, replace missing codes, find hours with no rows, and spot stations absent from the trips.

steps.title: Setup: library(tidyverse), library(readxl)

runs.purpose: load readxl, which reads Excel files

steps.explain: tidyr and dplyr, from the tidyverse, have the functions for missing values; readxl reads the depots' maintenance workbook.

steps.title: Blanks that mean "same as above": fill()

runs.purpose: read the maintenance workbook's summary sheet into `depot_months`
runs.task: Read the "Summary" sheet of `data/maintenance.xlsx` into `depot_months` with `read_excel()`.

runs.purpose: fill each depot's name down into the blank rows below it
runs.task: Fill `Depot` down into the missing rows with `fill()`.

steps.explain:
Whoever made the summary typed each depot's name once, on its January row, and left the rows below blank because they mean "same as above". Read in, those blanks are `NA`, yet the value is known.

`fill()` carries the last value down into the `NA`s below it, so each month is labelled with its depot; `.direction = "up"` would carry values up instead.

steps.title: A code for missing: na_if()

runs.purpose: find the lowest temperature and wind speed
runs.task: Find the lowest `temp_c` (as `coldest`) and the lowest `wind_kmh` (as `calmest`) with `summarize()`.

runs.code:
weather <- weather |>
  mutate(temp_c = na_if(temp_c, -99), wind_kmh = na_if(wind_kmh, -99))
alternatives: weather = weather |> mutate(temp_c = if_else(temp_c == -99, NA, temp_c), wind_kmh = if_else(wind_kmh == -99, NA, wind_kmh))
runs.purpose: replace the sensor's -99 readings with NA, in both columns
runs.task: Replace -99 with `NA` in `temp_c` and in `wind_kmh` with `na_if()`, and store the result back in `weather`.

steps.explain:
A temperature of -99 °C and a wind of -99 km/h can't be real: the sensor writes -99 when it has no reading. A code like that is worse than a blank, because sums and means treat it as a number.

`na_if(x, -99)` turns every -99 into `NA`, here {n_sentinel} readings, after which `min()` would need `na.rm = TRUE` and give a believable coldest hour, {coldest} °C. Check a dataset's documentation, or its extreme values, for codes such as -99, 9999 or "n/a".

steps.title: A fallback for missing: coalesce()

runs.code:
stations |>
  mutate(january_name = coalesce(former_name, name), .keep = "used") |>
  filter(january_name != name)
alternatives: stations |> transmute(name, former_name, january_name = if_else(is.na(former_name), name, former_name)) |> filter(january_name != name)
runs.purpose: find each station's name at the start of 2025: its former name if it has one, otherwise its name
runs.task: Add `january_name`: `former_name` where there is one, and `name` where it's missing, with `coalesce()`. Keep the columns used, and show the rows where it differs from `name`.

steps.explain:
Two stations were renamed during 2025, and `former_name` holds their old names; for every other station it is `NA`. `coalesce()` takes the first value that isn't missing, row by row, from the vectors it's given: the former name if there is one, otherwise the current name.

So `january_name` is what each station was called at the start of the year, and only the two renamed stations differ.

steps.title: Rows that aren't there: complete()

runs.code:
june <- weather |>
  filter(month(time) == 6) |>
  complete(time = seq(min(time), max(time), by = "hour"))
alternatives: june = weather |> filter(month(time) == 6) |> complete(time = seq(min(time), max(time), by = '1 hour'))
runs.purpose: keep June's hours and add a row for every hour the sensor missed, as `june`
runs.task: Keep June's rows (`month(time) == 6`), then add a row for every missing hour with `complete()` and `time = seq(min(time), max(time), by = "hour")`. Store the result in `june`.

runs.purpose: show June's hours with no temperature
runs.task: Keep the rows of `june` whose `temp_c` is missing.

steps.explain:
A visible missing value is an `NA` in a row. Another kind of missing value is a row that is absent. June has 720 hours, but `weather` has only {n_june} rows: the sensor stopped for a while.

`complete()` makes the missing rows, one for every value of `time` in the sequence that has no row yet, and fills their other columns with `NA`. That added {n_added} rows, and now the gap shows: from 23 June to 25 June, all of 24 June included.

steps.title: Nothing to average: NaN

runs.code:
june |>
  mutate(day = as_date(time)) |>
  summarize(mean_temp = mean(temp_c, na.rm = TRUE), .by = day) |>
  filter(is.nan(mean_temp))
alternatives: june |> group_by(day = as_date(time)) |> summarize(mean_temp = mean(temp_c, na.rm = TRUE)) |> filter(is.nan(mean_temp))
runs.purpose: average each June day's temperature, leaving out missing hours, and show the days whose mean isn't a number
runs.task: Add `day` (`as_date(time)`), find the mean `temp_c` for each day with `na.rm = TRUE`, then keep the days whose mean `is.nan()`.

steps.explain:
With `na.rm = TRUE`, `mean()` leaves out the missing hours. On 24 June every hour is missing, so the mean is of nothing at all, 0 divided by 0, which R calls `NaN`, "not a number". `NaN` behaves like `NA`, and `is.na()` is `TRUE` for both; `is.nan()` picks out only `NaN`.

Seeing one usually means a group had no values left to summarise.

steps.title: Missing groups: anti_join() and .drop

runs.purpose: find the stations that no trip started from
runs.task: Keep the stations with no trips starting from them, with `anti_join()` and `join_by(station_id == start_station)`.

runs.code:
trips |>
  mutate(
    start_station = factor(start_station, levels = unique(stations$station_id))
  ) |>
  count(start_station, .drop = FALSE) |>
  filter(n == 0)
alternatives: trips |> mutate(start_station = factor(start_station, levels = unique(stations$station_id))) |> count(start_station, .drop = FALSE) |> filter(n < 1)
runs.purpose: count the trips from every station in the registry, keeping stations with none
runs.task: Make `start_station` a factor with every registry station (`unique(stations$station_id)`) as a level. Count with `.drop = FALSE` and keep counts of 0.

steps.explain:
A count only has rows for values that occur, so a station with no trips is simply absent from `count(trips, start_station)`. `anti_join()` finds them by comparison: the stations with no matching trip, the two in Saltings.

A factor knows its possible values even when they don't occur, and `.drop = FALSE` keeps a row for each, with a count of 0. Either way, a missing group becomes something you can see.
